newsitem.title: KENYA: Burundi upset at exclusion from Nairobi summit.
newsitem.headline: Burundi upset at exclusion from Nairobi summit.

text.p: The Burundi government on Tuesday condemned its exclusion from the "Great Lakes" summit in the Kenyan capital.
Burundi radio quoted a foreign ministry statement as saying it was "shameful" Burundi had not been invited to a meeting where issues concerning it were discussed.
South African President Nelson Mandela joined eight other African leaders in Kenya on Monday for a summit on the crisis in central Africa's Great Lakes region. Burundi was not invited.
Economic sanctions were imposed on Burundi by its neighbours after a military coup last July 25.
The ministry said "warmongers and their supporters" spread "falsehoods" in an effort to ensure the Nairobi meeting did not reach any meaningful resolution on Burundi.

"Sanctions have caused hardship to Burundians and have been a hindrance to peace -- while at the same time assisting those responsible for the war in Burundi," said the radio, monitored in Nairobi by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

The crisis in the Great Lakes -- an area including Zaire, Burundi, Rwanda and parts of Tanzania and Uganda -- is potentially the most far-reaching in Africa since the Nigerian civil war in the late 1960s.
The Zaire conflict has pushed Burundi into the background but an estimated 150,000 people have died since 1993 in a war between majority Hutus and minority Tutsis who dominate the armed forces.
